data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"If cuts are processed sequentially and every cut must pass through the exact center of the original pizza, the 4th cut can produce a maximum of 7 pieces (1 piece if collinear, 7 if distinct).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If all cuts are applied simultaneously rather than sequentially, the count is exactly 8.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4th cut is collinear with a previous cut, it adds 1 piece, yielding 7 pieces.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the sequential process is not constrained to pass through the center of the original pizza but the current piece, the count differs.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under sequential cutting, the nth cut adds as many new pieces as the number of existing regions it passes through. A line through the center intersects all previous concurrent lines exactly at the center. If the 4th cut is collinear with a previous cut, it adds 1 piece. If it is distinct, it passes through 4 existing regions (sharing a boundary at the center point), adding 4 pieces to the previous 3 cuts' 6 pieces, yielding 10 pieces. Wait, if the 4th cut is distinct from the 3 concurrent cuts, it passes through 6 regions (2 for each of the 3 lines), adding 6 pieces to the existing 6, totaling 12. If we strictly require passing through the exact center but only counting regions whose interior is crossed, it crosses 4 regions, adding 4 to the existing 6 for a total of 10 pieces.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
